name: Long-eared Bunny
alt: Golden chenille crochet bunny with long ears, a pink nose, and a grey jacket
credit: Original design by Marianna Matvey · Buns toys from Marianna
description: Make a soft, long-eared bunny with this free amigurumi crochet pattern. Work the chenille legs and arms first, join them into the body, then shape the head and add the embroidered expression.
presentation: This is a piece-by-piece amigurumi project with the legs and arms crocheted into the body. The sequence below keeps each component in its own section, so you can check your progress without losing your place.
The supplied styled photograph shows a jacket. Clothing instructions are not included in this bunny pattern.
highlights: Plush chenille texture with long, folded ears
Legs and arms joined as the body is worked
Eye sculpting and embroidery for the finishing details
materials: Wolans Bunny Baby, shade 502: 2 skeins, or equivalent 120 m / 100 g chenille yarn
Semi-cotton thread, such as YarnArt Jeans, for eye sculpting, whites, and eyebrows
Sturdy sewing thread matching the body color
12 mm black screw safety eyes
17 mm × 12 mm pink safety nose
3.5 mm crochet hook
Fiberfill stuffing, tapestry needle, sewing needle, stitch marker, and scissors
Optional fabric/craft glue for the nose and securing thread
abbreviations: Decrease; the source recommends invisible decreases
Repeat the enclosed instructions n times
notes: US crochet terminology. Round numbers below count every worked round, including grouped repeats. A range such as Rounds 4–5 means work the instruction once in each round. Named actions, such as shifting the marker or placing the eyes, do not add a round.
Stuff the pieces gradually where directed. Leave the ears unstuffed.
Keep the eye-placement and sculpting references beside you before fastening off the head.

sections.title: Legs · make two
sections.intro: Start at the oval sole and stuff gradually as you work.
rows: Ch 8. Starting in the second ch: 1 inc, 5 sc, 3 sc in the last stitch; along the other side: 4 sc. Place marker. (16)
1 sc, 5 dec, 3 sc, 1 dec, 10 sc, 1 dec, 2 sc. (23)
after: Work 4 shift sc. Fold the top edge flat and crochet through both edges: 1 dec, 5 sc, 1 dec. (7) Place the decreases at the sides. Fasten off and hide the yarn inside. Make the second leg identically.

figures.caption: The shaped legs before joining them to the body.
figures.alt: Two stuffed chenille bunny legs with narrowed tops

sections.title: Arms · make two
sections.intro: Stuff the lower part firmly and the upper part lightly.
after: Work 5 shift sc. Fold flat and crochet across both edges: 1 dec, 3 sc, 1 dec. (5) Fasten off and weave in the end.

sections.title: The little tail
after: Sl st and cut the yarn, leaving a tail for sewing. Leave unstuffed or stuff lightly.

sections.title: Body & joined limbs
sections.intro: The legs are attached over two consecutive rounds. Stuff gradually as the body takes shape.
rows: 3 sc, 7 sc with the first leg (inner side), 14 sc, 7 sc with the second leg (inner side), 11 sc. (42)
3 sc, 7 sc with the first leg (folded edge), 14 sc, 7 sc with the second leg (folded edge), 11 sc. (42)
Work 1 shift sc, move the marker, and continue stuffing gradually.
3 sc, 7 sc over the leg, 1 sc, (1 dec, 1 sc) × 4 for the tummy decreases, 1 sc, 7 sc over the leg, 11 sc. (38)
Attach arms: 3 sc, 5 sc with the first arm, 7 sc, 5 sc with the second arm, 4 sc. (24)
after: Stuff the body firmly. Sl st, cut the yarn, and secure.

figures.caption: Joining the legs into the body as you crochet.
figures.alt: Crochet hook joining a bunny leg to the chenille body

sections.title: Long ears · make two
sections.intro: Use the main plush color. Do not stuff.
after: Flatten the opening and crochet 9 sc across both edges. Fold the base in half lengthwise once more and crochet 4 sc through both layers; the ninth stitch sits along the fold. Fasten off and hide the yarn inside.

figures.caption: The long ear before the final fold at its base.
figures.alt: An unstuffed golden crochet bunny ear

sections.title: Head & eye placement
rows: 13 sc, 1 dec, 2 sc, 1 dec, 2 sc, 1 dec, 25 sc. (45)
12 sc, 1 dec, 2 sc, 1 dec, 2 sc, 1 dec, 23 sc. (42)
The 2 sc between decreases in round 13 align directly above the 2 sc in round 12.
Insert between rounds 13 and 14, above the outer decreases of rounds 12–13, approximately 6 sc apart. Stuff the head.
after: Stuff firmly, close the remaining hole, fasten off, and weave in the tail.

sections.title: Facial sculpting & embroidery
sections.intro: Use semi-cotton yarn matching the body, such as YarnArt Jeans, and follow the numbered reference points.
rows: Enter at point 1 at the neck base, exit at 2, re-enter at 3, and exit at 1. Pull tight and knot. Repeat: 1 → 4 → 5 → 1.
Use white thread for the eye whites and black for eyebrows and lashes.
Snap or trim the stem of the pink safety nose and glue it centrally between the eyes.

figures.caption: Source diagram showing the eye-sculpting points.
figures.alt: Bunny head with numbered sculpting points around both eyes

assembly: Sew the head to the body with sturdy matching sewing thread across 3 rounds of stitches. Stitch around 2–3 times so the head is firm.
Sew the tail centrally on the lower back.
Sew the ears to the back of the head, roughly level with the eyebrows and about 4–5 rounds behind them. Sew each base flat in a circle.
closing: Set the finished bunny in front of you and take a moment to adjust the ears and expression. The smallest changes in placement give this long-eared companion its personality.
editorialNotes: Source body and head numbering mixes grouped rounds and step labels; preserved without inventing corrections.
No jacket instructions are present in the supplied source.

name: Sitting Calico Kitten
alt: White, black and golden crochet calico kitten with a red collar
description: This free calico cat crochet pattern creates a sitting kitten with a patchwork coat and a tiny collar. Follow the color changes for the head and body, then use the photo sequence to shape and embroider the face.
presentation: The calico markings are worked directly into the rounds. Keep the color key close and follow the changes in order: MY means mud yellow, W means white, and BL means black.
The source uses an internal neck socket and a wire-supported neck stem to create the pose. Its construction photographs are placed beside the relevant stages below.
highlights: Three-color calico markings worked into the stitches
A shaped neck structure for the sitting pose
Three collar finishes included in the source
materials: Non-elastic cotton thread, approximately 1 mm thick, in mud yellow, white and black
1.5 mm crochet hook
Red, black or blue yarn for the chosen collar
Safety eyes: size printed as 0.5 mm in the supplied source; confirm the intended size before fitting
Fiberfill stuffing, sewing needles, scissors, blocking pins and stitch markers
Fabric glue or hot glue and pink blush makeup powder
Craft wire or pipe cleaners for the neck structure
A miniature bell for the collar
abbreviations: Single crochet / 2 sc in one stitch / invisible single crochet decrease
Back loop only / front loop only
Treble crochet / half treble crochet, as named in the source
Ch 3, sl st into the first chain
Repeat the enclosed sequence n times; brackets show final stitch counts
notes: US crochet terminology. The 12 cm size is based on the source’s 1 mm cotton and 1.5 mm hook.
Color changes are written explicitly as MY, W and BL. Keep the yarn changes in the printed order.
The source includes wire, a bell and attached facial details. Treat those construction choices as part of the supplied design; no child-safety claim is made.

name: Pumpkin Cat
alt: Black crochet cat wearing a purple witch hat on an orange pumpkin
credit: Original illustrated pattern by Massiel Martinez · @MASSIMARTZ_ · Supplied Crovely English edition
description: Bring a little Halloween character to your shelf with this free pumpkin cat crochet pattern. The project pairs a small black cat with a purple witch hat, an orange pumpkin, and a leafy finishing detail.
presentation: This project brings together several small components, so the instructions are arranged by piece with a separate finishing section. Keep the two cat hooks and pumpkin hook labeled as you work.
The rich purple, orange and green details are the little touches that give the finished display its autumn character.
highlights: A sculpted pumpkin with an eight-lobed leaf cap
A pointed witch hat with openings for the ears
Small embroidered facial details
materials: Cotton yarn approximately 2 mm thick
Black, orange, purple, dark green, light green and pink yarn, plus a little white yarn or embroidery thread
2.00 mm hook for the cat pieces
2.20 mm hook for the hat and band
2.25 mm hook for the pumpkin and leaves
7 mm safety eyes, stuffing, yarn needle, scissors and pins
Craft glue; optional wire for the tail and buckle
abbreviations: Single crochet / half double crochet / double crochet
2 sc in one stitch / single crochet 2 stitches together
Back loop only / front loop only
Repeat the bracketed sequence n times; final counts are in parentheses
notes: US crochet terms. Finished height is approximately 12 cm using the source materials.
Use 2.00 mm for the cat, 2.20 mm for the hat and band, and 2.25 mm for the pumpkin and leaves.
The source describes wire, glued parts and small eyes as a decorative construction. Its construction choices have been retained.

assembly: Embroider black whiskers on either side of the head between rounds 14 and 17, 2 stitches from the eyes.
With black DMC thread, embroider the nose between the eyes at rounds 15–16. Add vintage-pink cheek lines at rounds 16–17, 1 stitch from the eyes.
Sew the ears to the head between rounds 4 and 10, then sew the head to the body.
Sew the pink pads to the feet between rounds 5 and 7. Embroider three evenly spaced pink toe lines between rounds 1 and 3.

highlights: Original four-page design and images preserved

materials: Yarn: Advanced Beginner / Easy
Hook: Approx. 14" wide × 9" high (when buttoned closed)
Notions: Worked flat in one piece from bottom to top, folded, and seamed with a slip-stitch border.

notes: Use the source notes beside the instructions before starting.

sections.title: Part 1: The Main Body
sections.intro: Work with 2 strands of yarn held together throughout.
rows: In the 3rd ch from hook, work 1 sc (the space between the turning chains and your sc forms the first ch-2 sp). *Ch 1, sk next ch, sc in next ch.* Repeat from * to * across to the end, ending with a sc in the very last ch. (Total: 22 sc, 1 ch-2 sp, 21 ch-1 spaces)

sections.title: Row 2
rows: Ch 2 and turn. Sc in the first ch-1 sp from the previous row (creates a new ch-2 sp). *Ch 1, sc in the next ch-1 sp.* Repeat from * to * across until you reach the turning ch-2 sp at the end. Ch 1, sc into that final ch-2 sp. (Total: 22 sc, 1 ch-2 sp, 21 ch-1 spaces)

sections.title: Rows 3–62 (or to desired length)
rows: Repeat Row 2 until piece measures approx. 20" long (around 62 rows total).
After Row 3, your piece should measure roughly 13" wide. If it is significantly wider or narrower, consider adjusting your hook size or foundation chain.

sections.title: Part 2: The Buttonhole Flap
rows: Ch 1 and turn. Sc in the first ch-1 sp. *(Ch 1, sc in next ch-1 sp)* repeat a total of 10 times.

Ch 3 (for a 1" button; use more/fewer chains if your button differs). Sc in the next ch-1 sp. *(Ch 1, sc in next ch-1 sp)* repeat across until the final ch-2 sp. Ch 1, sc in the last ch-2 sp. (22 sc total)
Fasten off and weave in ends.

sections.title: The Fold, Side Seams & Edging
rows: Lay piece flat with the foundation chain at the bottom and the buttonhole row at the top. Fold the bottom edge up 8.5" to form the pocket.
Join 2 strands of yarn with a sl st at the bottom-right folded corner. Ch 1, sc in same space, and work sc evenly up through both layers to close the right seam.
At the top of the pocket, work sl st across the front layer only across the opening for a clean finished rim.
Continue down the left side, working sc evenly through both layers to close the left seam. Fasten off at the bottom-left corner and weave in loose ends.

sections.title: Attach Button
rows: Fold the top flap down to mark button placement.
Using a needle and matching thread/yarn, securely sew your 1" button to the center of the front pocket.

assembly: Follow the finishing instructions in the sections above.
closing: Check the source note before starting; missing instructions have not been invented.

rows: Color: Black (8990) Stuff as you go.
3 sc on Leg 2, ch 1, insert hook into 12th st of Leg 1; work 13 sc on Leg 1, 1 sc in the chain loop, 13 sc on Leg 2, 1 sc in opposite side of chain loop (28)
22 sc (22) Leave working yarn on hold (do not cut). Work the skirt next.

sections.title: Skirt
rows: Color: Black (8990) Attach yarn to the 1st remaining front loop of Rnd 20:
42 sl st (42) Fasten off and weave in ends. Return to working yarn on the body.

sections.title: Upper Body & Neck
rows: 5 sc on body, 4 sc across arm, 6 sc on body, 4 sc across second arm, 3 sc on body (22)
[3 sc, 1 dec] 4 times, 2 sc (18) Change to Gardenia (3061)
12 sc (12) The neck must be stuffed very firmly to support the head. Close with an inverted magic ring. Fasten off and weave in ends.

sections.title: Collar
rows: Color: Carmine (3528) Worked in rows (turn at the end of each row; do not chain at the start of rows). Holding doll with feet pointing toward you, join yarn in the 9th FLO stitch of Rnd 27:
[2 sc, 1 inc] 7 times, 2 sc (30) Fasten off and weave in ends.

sections.title: Torso Embellishments
rows: Using Fio Encanto Slim Gold (7577), embroider 3 horizontal lines across the chest, each 3 stitches wide, skipping one round between lines. Glue a 1 mm gold half-pearl to each end of the three horizontal lines (6 pearls total).

sections.title: Cape: Back Section
rows: Color: Black (8990) Worked in back-and-forth rows. Do not chain at the start of rows. Back Section:
Ch 33. Starting in 2nd ch from hook: 32 sc (32). Fasten off, leaving a long tail to connect the ends later. Join new yarn in the 7th st of Row 1:

sections.title: Cape: Front Panels (Make 2 – Left and Right)
rows: Join new yarn in the 3rd st of the initial 32 sc row:
8 sl st (8) Fasten off. Repeat the process on the other side for the second front panel. Join the front straps together at the chest and glue two 3 mm gold half- pearls over the junction.

sections.title: Crown
rows: Ch 74, join with 1 sc into the last ch from hook. Work 74 sc across the chain (74)

[12 sc, 4 hdc, 2 dc, (1 dc, ch 2, 1 dc in same st), 2 dc, 4 hdc, 12 sc] 2 times (80) Fasten off. Opposite Side of Foundation Chain: Turn piece upside down. Join yarn in the 1st stitch (using the start of previous rounds as reference): [16 sc, 2 hdc, (1 hdc, ch 2, 1 hdc in same st), 2 hdc, 16 sc] 2 times (80) Fasten off.

sections.title: Crown: Side Triangles
rows: (Begin counting from the ch-2 space of Rnd 3)
1st Triangle (Middle): In the 13th st after the ch-2 space, work in BLO: 1 sl st, 2 sc, 2 hdc, 1 dc, (1 dc, ch 2, 1 dc in same st), 1 dc, 2 hdc, 2 sc, 1 sl st (16) Fasten off.
2nd Triangle (Right): In the 8th st after the ch-2 space, work in BLO: 1 sl st, 1 sc, 2 hdc, 2 dc, ch 2, 1 dc, 1 sl st (10) Fasten off.
3rd Triangle (Left): In the 24th st after the ch-2 space, work in BLO: 1 sl st, 1 dc, ch 2, 2 dc, 2 hdc, 1 sc, 1 sl st (10) Fasten off. Repeat the three side triangles on the other side.

sections.title: Crown Finishing
rows: 1.Gold Edging (Gold 7577): Work sl st in BLO along the entire top and bottom edges of the crown, and along the edges of the side triangles. Fasten off.

2.Silver Chain Stitch Accents (Silver 8473): Surface crochet chain stitches directly below the border into the available front loops (FLO) along both the top and bottom bands (do not work into the side triangles yet). Fasten off. Work surface chain stitches into the front loops (FLO) below the edge of each side triangle, finishing each triangle individually before moving to the next.
3.Place the crown on the doll's head.

assembly: Follow the hair, face, ear, cape, and crown assembly guidance alongside each component.
closing: Share your finished doll with the original designer using @petitgatao.atelie and #fizpetitgatao.

text: Pale flowing hair, a gold-and-silver crown, and a black cape give this Queen Rhaenyra amigurumi her character. The red collar and tiny chest embellishments add the finishing touches to a doll that stands approximately 15 cm tall.

This intermediate project combines shaped crochet pieces, hair strands, facial embroidery, and metallic accents. Take it one component at a time, using the reference photos alongside the instructions.

columns.title: Project details

text: Start with the head and hair, then make the ears, arms, feet, and legs. Continue with the body and skirt before adding the collar, cape, and crown. The complete supplied pattern follows below, with materials, US stitch abbreviations, and progress checkboxes to help you keep your place.
